ai.description: This gecko reaches 40 mm SVL. It is brown with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Key features include a rounded snout and granular dorsal scales with scattered tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Cnemaspis kolhapurensis* is the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on the throat, which is absent in similar sympatric species.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis kolhapurensis* inhabits rocky outcrops and boulders within moist deciduous forests in the Northern Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 500 and 800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kolhapur Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging after sunset to actively hunt insects on vertical rock surfaces and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis kolhapurensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis kolhapurensis* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
